chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a Mudabbir (slave promised freedom upon his master's death) who killed a man deliberately, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is killed due to it.' I said: 'And if he killed him by error?' He said: 'He is handed over to the guardians of the killed one, so he becomes a slave for them; if they wish, they can sell him, and if they wish, they can keep him, and it is not for them to kill him.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! The Mudabbir is a slave.'

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: Awliya' al-maqtul: The guardians/heirs of the killed person.
key_terms.اسْتَرَقُّوهُ: Istarraqoohu: To keep him as a slave (from the root of slavery).
key_terms.مُدَبَّر: Mudabbir: A slave whose master has declared he will be freed upon the master's death.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status and punishment for a Mudabbir who kills a free man in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juridical status of a 'Mudabbir' as a full slave for the purpose of blood money and retribution, distinguishing his liability from that of a free man. It establishes that while intentional murder warrants execution, accidental killing results in the Mudabbir becoming the property of the victim's heirs, who hold the option to either manumit him via sale or retain his servitude, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the master's discretion in such compensatory arrangements.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the ‘Mudabbir’ (slave promised freedom upon the death of his master), who killed a man deliberately. So heasws said: ‘He would be killed due to it’. I said, ‘So if he killed him in error?’ So heasws said: ‘He would be handed over to the guardians of the killed one, so he would happen to be a slave for them, if  they so desire to they can sell him, and if they so desire to they can keep him, and it is not for them that they kill him’.
Then heasws said: ‘O Abu Muhammad! The ‘Mudabbir’ is a slave’.
